file.content:
OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            Optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            4-digit code that is valid for the city's region via the fixed table
            (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099); a city with no known
            region accepts any 4-digit postcode. Stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized by
            stripping every non-digit character and must contain exactly 10 digits.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            Optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a
            syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            Optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When present, an 'ageBand' is derived from it as of the registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner has the
            same last name at the same address (i.e. they share a household).
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID

## What I did

I read the change context — a structured address form (`addressLine1`/optional `addressLine2`/`city`/`postcode`) preferred over the flat `address`, with normalization + a composed `address` string — and traced where its complexity lands. Then I restructured *only* the existing code, following this codebase's idioms (small named seams; pure-string helpers like `AddressNormalizer`; per-concept isolation), so the change edits small methods rather than bloating anything.

**`BuildOwner` (create path)** — `service` was one long method mixing address normalization, presence checks, telephone/email normalization, mapping, and date logic. I split out the two pieces the change rewrites:
- `canonicalizeAddress(request)` — the single seam that normalizes the supplied address and writes the canonical form back onto the request. The change extends *this* to normalize the structured fields and compose the `address` string, instead of threading that through `service`.
- `requireFields(request, normalizedAddress)` — the presence rule in one place. The change relaxes *this* to "valid with an address in either form, plus city." It already receives the whole `request`, so it can inspect `addressLine1` without a new signature.

**`ApplyOwner` (update path)** — grouped the three address-related setters into an `applyAddress(owner, request)` seam, so structured-field application + composition land there rather than swelling the flat setter list in `service`.

**`AddressNormalizer` and `Owner`** — deliberately left untouched. `AddressNormalizer` is already "the single home for owner address normalization" and is the natural, ready home for the new pure-string `compose(...)`. Keeping composition in that helper and in the write-path seams is exactly what keeps `Owner`'s new `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` accessors trivial — preventing the composition logic from leaking into the entity's getters/setters (which is where the "direct" implementation apparently over-loaded them).

All edits are pure extractions with identical behavior (setter reordering among independent fields; moving the address write-back ahead of a throw that discards the request either way), verified by the unchanged test outcome.
